newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-MATCHES IN GERMAN LEAGUE CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MATCHES IN GERMAN LEAGUE CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Matches scheduled for this weekend in the German league championship. League positions in parentheses.

First meeting this season between last season's surprise sides. Leverkusen bouyed by 3-2 win over Bochum in midweek and likely to welcome back defender Christian Woerns from injury. Stuttgart still looking for first win after two draws to start their new campaign.

Derby between two clubs from Ruhr Valley industrial region likely to be fiercely contested. Duisburg, however, also likely to have half an eye on next week's Intertoto Cup final against former French champions Auxerre.

Karlsruhe dogged by controversy after salvaging a draw thanks to a late goal against 1860 Munich in midweek. The Munich club says the referee blew for a free kick just before Sean Dundee's strike and television replays appear to confirm that version of events. The match may have to be replayed.

Another Ruhr Valley derby and also battle of Germany's European title winners. Schalke captain and libero Olaf Thon doubtful, complaining of pains in his arms and ribs after midweek match against Duisburg. Striker Stephane Chapuisat, who missed Wednesday's game against Cologne as he was playing for Switzerland, available again for Dortmund.

Early-season leaders Kaiserslautern have no major injury problems. Main difficulty for coach Otto Rehhagel is dampening euophoria after two straight wins on the promoted club's return to the top flight. Cologne coach Peter Neururer under pressure after peformance in Dortmund almost as unattractive as the club's new red and orange shirts.

Match which underscores topsy-turvy nature of early-season table with champions Bayern anchored near the bottom and promoted Wolfsburg close to the top. Bayern, with only a draw and a defeat to their name so far, will be keen to record their first win of the season and prevent an early gap opening up between them and title rivals such as Leverkusen and Dortmund.

No major injury worries for either side, who are both still looking for their first win. 1860 top scorer Berhard Winkler was taken off against Karlsruhe after spitting up blood but medical check revealed only a minor blood vessel burst and he will be available to take on Bremen.

Polish striker Slawomir Majak doubtful for Rostock with a thigh injury. Hamburg coach Frank Pagelsdorf looking to move up a gear after two solid draws in his first league games at the helm of his new club.

Berlin hoping for another big crowd after more than 75,000 turned out at the Olympic Stadium to watch the promoted home side take on Dortmund. Both Hertha and Moenchengladbach looking to post their first win of the campaign.
